A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GP-CFM research despite the changed title. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 and Appendix E report original Gaussian-mixture simulations and MNIST/HWD+ experiments, including repeated-run Wasserstein, KID and FID results.

after.justification: The retained experiments are supplemented by original CIFAR-10 quality and timing results, intermediate-distribution analyses and an application to mouse-brain LFP recordings.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains joint GP sampling of positions and velocities, the squared-error stream objective, endpoint coupling and optional starting-point conditioning. Revised notation, covariate terminology and additional applications do not introduce a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: v5 adds unconditional CIFAR-10 natural-image generation and multiregion mouse-brain time-series generation using one LFP recording session. Appendix F also introduces a two-Gaussian-to-three-Gaussian transformation scenario. The original MNIST, HWD+ and toy-data coverage remains.

E2.justification: The existing standard-Gaussian-to-two-Gaussian comparison expands from I-CFM and GP-I-CFM in v1 Figure 1B to include OT-CFM and GP-OT-CFM in v5 Table 1. These methods already participated in the MNIST comparison, whose comparator membership remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce substantial protocols: CIFAR-10 uses a 128-channel U-Net, batch size 128, specified noise controls, DOPRI5 sampling, FID from 50,000 generated images and timed ten-image batches. The LFP application uses 214 trials, seven regions and five selected time points from 50, with rescaled time. These are new experimental settings; the retained MNIST/HWD+ architectures and HWD+ split remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix F and Figure 7 add a focused comparison of intermediate distributions, testing whether GP streams suppress spurious modes during a two-to-three-Gaussian transformation. Appendix I also reports LFP runtime with five versus 50 time points. The existing variance-schedule and crossing-stream/covariate analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The existing 100-run experiments retain mean and standard-error reporting. v5 Table 4 adds a distinct repeated-evaluation procedure: each trained CIFAR-10 model undergoes 20 FID evaluations and 20 generation-timing measurements, summarized by means and standard errors. These are repeated evaluations of trained models, not 20 independent training runs.

E6.justification: For the retained Gaussian-mixture setting, I-CFM/GP-I-CFM Wasserstein means change from 1.51/1.27 in v1 Figure 1B to 1.54/1.51 in v5 Table 1. New CIFAR-10 FIDs are 3.75, 3.74, 3.62 and 3.75 for I-CFM, OT-CFM, GP-I-CFM and GP-OT-CFM, respectively, alongside timing results. Intermediate-mode and LFP findings are added, while MNIST means and variance-schedule scores are retained.

T1.justification: The Bayesian squared-error justification, GP conditioning and derivative formulas, linear-kernel reduction, and three continuity/gradient-equivalence proofs remain substantively the same. The Bayesian argument moves to Appendix A, and v1 Theorems 1–3 become v5 Propositions 1–3 in Appendix J. Notation and regularity-condition wording change without a substantive new derivation or result.

C1.justification: The central claims of simulation-free GP-stream training, variance reduction and integration of correlated observations persist. v5 adds explicit claims about smoother fields, computationally efficient generation, irregularly spaced observations and complementarity with endpoint coupling. The Bayesian perspective ceases to be a headline contribution but remains part of the paper.

C2.justification: v5 expands the mechanism account to suppression of spurious intermediate modes and easier numerical integration. It interprets CIFAR-10 results as suggesting limitations of high-dimensional minibatch OT and acknowledges that combining OT with GP streams need not improve performance. Conversely, v1's explicit complete-observation requirement and proposed latent-space remedy disappear, without a demonstrated missing-data solution. Appendix I adds a biological interpretation of the generated LFP trajectories.

D1.justification: v5 supplies hardware specifications and training timings for retained applications, plus CIFAR-10 optimizer, clipping, EMA, noise, solver and clean-fid details. It also documents LFP selection, temporal subsampling, rescaling and runtime. These substantially expand implementation and reproducibility information; the code-access link remains the same.

R1.justification: v5 explicitly positions GP-CFM as extending stochastic interpolants and acknowledges multimarginal work by Albergo and colleagues, qualifying v1's assertion that existing FM methods only accommodate endpoints. It also credits earlier covariate/guided-flow methods by Isobe and Zheng and removes several diffusion/latent-model references. This revises the novelty context beyond a bibliographic update.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and conclusion are substantially recast. Section 2 becomes Background and Notation, much of the Bayesian argument moves to Appendix A, applications are organized by purpose, and proofs are consolidated under Appendix J. Stream notation and related/labeled terminology are revised throughout.

P2.justification: Numerical panels embedded in v1 Figures 1, 2, 5 and 7 become standalone tables in v5. Plots are resized or rearranged, HWD+ image traces move to Appendix Figure 9B, and the MNIST sample-image panel is removed. New displays show intermediate modes, CIFAR-10 results and samples, and LFP trajectories.

improvement.justification: v1 supports its practical claims mainly through toy problems and handwritten digits, with little measured computational-cost evidence. v5 substantially strengthens that foundation through the CIFAR-10 quality/timing comparison, smoothing analysis, real time-series application and implementation disclosures. Clearer positioning against stochastic-interpolant and multimarginal research also improves the contribution's assessment. The LFP evidence remains descriptive, and removing the complete-observation caveat weakens limitation reporting, but these drawbacks do not outweigh the gains in empirical support and transparency.
